mechanism: An agent is handed a game one function at a time. Each attempted C function is compiled with the game's original compiler and compared byte for byte with the original machine code, and only an exact match scores. That hard oracle stops the model bluffing and lets it iterate until it matches. It runs locally on Linux (compilers are Linux programs) and needs the user's own ROM.
claim: Point your own agent at a game you own and it produces C that rebuilds to identical bytes, with 245 public projects to continue.
why_not_testable: Linux and Windows only (not macOS), needs a game ROM and the project is archived.
needs: A Linux box and a legally owned ROM.
one_line: A byte-exact compiler check turns decompiling into a game the agent cannot cheat, and the author archived it after community pushback.
idea_why: An exact-match verifier is the strongest kind of feedback loop for an agent, whatever the domain.
breakdown: The pattern is: pick a task with a cheap exact oracle, give the agent a tool to submit attempts, and score only on a perfect match. For decompilation that means the matching compiler plus a diff of the object file. Reuse the idea elsewhere, for example matching generated output against a reference hash. A person is needed for ROM dumps and for community norms, since many decomp projects reject AI contributions.
